prompt: Shops should not be allowed to sell any food or drink that are scientifically proven to be bad for health. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
essay:
Some people argue that shops should not sell junk food or energy drinks, which are linked to diabetes and high blood pressure. As a result, these products can contribute to serious illness and long-term disability. I half agree with this statement, because such food causes health problems when eaten regularly.

Eating junk food can be highly addictive and most people do not notice it because it is normalised. I think the government should tax junk food and run advertising campaigns to encourage people to make healthier choices. Higher prices tend to change buying habits, as many people reconsider a daily purchase once it becomes noticeably more expensive. A complete ban would be difficult to enforce, since people would simply buy these products elsewhere or turn to unregulated sellers. Society has contributed to this problem, since life moves quickly and many people do not have the time to cook. Banning these products would leave them with fewer options rather than better ones.

Restrictions can be justified in some cases. Energy drinks, for example, should not be sold to children, in the same way that alcohol and tobacco are already age-restricted. Children are still growing, and large amounts of caffeine can affect their sleep and concentration at school. Age limits are therefore the best approach, since these drinks are addictive.

In conclusion, I partly agree with this statement. Banning unhealthy products entirely would be impractical, but age restrictions on energy drinks, combined with taxation and public health campaigns, would be a more effective approach.
